title: Ethiopian Berbere Beef with Onions and Green Chillies
summary: Cubes of beef are seared hard and fast, then tossed through onions, garlic, ginger and green chillies with a warm berbere spice blend for a quick, deeply savoury sauté.
equipment: large heavy frying pan or cast-iron skillet (30 cm)

ingredients.note: use half for a milder dish

ingredients.item: beef sirloin (or rump), trimmed, cut into 2.5 cm cubes
fine sea salt or table salt
medium onions, cut into 2 cm wedges, layers separated
long green chillies (or jalapeños), cut into strips

steps.title: Season the beef
steps.text: Mix the paprika, cayenne, ginger, fenugreek, coriander, cardamom, allspice and cloves together to make the berbere blend. Toss the beef cubes with the salt and half of this spice mix so the flavour begins working into the meat straight away.

steps.title: Sear in batches
steps.text: Heat the oil in a large frying pan over high heat until lightly smoking, then add half the beef in a single layer with space between the pieces. Leave it for 2-3 minutes until well seared underneath, turn, and sear for 1-2 minutes more before lifting it into a bowl and repeating with the second batch. The beef won't be cooked through at this stage; searing in batches keeps the pan hot enough to brown the meat properly instead of letting it stew in its own juices.

steps.title: Soften the onions
steps.text: Lower the heat to medium, add the ghee, onion wedges and rosemary sprigs, and cook for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the onions have softened and browned at the edges.

steps.title: Bloom the spices
steps.text: Stir in the garlic, ginger, chillies and the remaining berbere and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Letting the spice mix sizzle briefly in the hot ghee draws out far more aroma than adding it straight to a liquid would.

steps.title: Finish the beef
steps.text: Return the seared beef and its juices to the pan and toss for 2-3 minutes until everything is coated, sizzling, and a thermometer in the centre of the thickest cube reads 63°C. Take the pan off the heat and rest for 3 minutes, then stir in the lemon juice and lift out the rosemary sprigs. Resting lets the juices settle back into the meat before serving.

steps.title: Serve with injera
steps.text: Serve the tibs on injera, or with rice if you prefer, tearing off pieces of the flatbread to scoop up the spiced beef and onions. The slightly sour, spongy injera is traditionally used instead of cutlery.

tips: Make sure the pan is really hot before adding the beef, and don't crowd it, or the meat will steam rather than sear.
A common mistake is adding all the spice at once; frying the second half of the berbere in ghee with the aromatics gives a deeper, less raw flavour.
Wear gloves or wash your hands well after handling the chillies.
Check the beef's temperature with a probe thermometer rather than guessing by colour, especially with smaller cubes.
Leave the rosemary sprigs whole rather than chopping the leaves in, so they're easy to remove later.
storage: Cool leftovers within 2 hours, refrigerate for up to 3 days, and reheat in a hot pan until piping hot (74°C) throughout before serving.
